summary: Polygon's staff ranks its top 50 movies of 2023, built from individual staff ballots weighted by strength of opinion so mainstream hits don't overpower underseen indies. The intro frames the year around the Barbenheimer phenomenon, which showed that great, passionately told stories stand out regardless of genre. Oppenheimer takes the top spot, followed by Past Lives and The Holdovers, with each entry including director, cast, where to watch and a short blurb.
one_line: Polygon's staff-voted ranking of the 50 best movies of 2023, topped by Christopher Nolan's Oppenheimer, with Barbenheimer as the year's defining story.
key_facts: Polygon's list is built from individual staff ballots, ranked numerically or weighted, and combined into a collective list weighted by strength of opinion so a much-seen mainstream movie doesn't have too much advantage over an underseen indie.
Any movie released in the US during the calendar year is eligible, but because the list was published in early December, some December releases are underrepresented.

The intro cites the Barbenheimer phenomenon, in which film fans saw Barbie and Oppenheimer back-to-back, as a boost for beleaguered movie theaters and as proof that a great story stands out regardless of tone or topic.

Oppenheimer, directed by Christopher Nolan and starring Cillian Murphy, Robert Downey Jr. and Florence Pugh, is ranked #1; it draws on the biography American Prometheus and features a score by Ludwig Göransson.
Past Lives, directed by Celine Song and starring Greta Lee, Teo Yoo and John Magaro, is ranked #2; it unfolds across three time frames 12 years apart and was shot on 35mm by Shabier Kirchner.
The Holdovers, directed by Alexander Payne and starring Paul Giamatti, Da'Vine Joy Randolph and Dominic Sessa, is ranked #3; it is set at a 1970s boys' prep school at Christmas.
Killers of the Flower Moon, Martin Scorsese's 206-minute adaptation of David Grann's 2017 account of the Osage murders, is ranked #4.
Barbie, directed by Greta Gerwig with co-writer Noah Baumbach, is ranked #9; Ryan Gosling's 'I'm Just Ken' is called 2023's top movie anthem.
Spider-Man: Across the Spider-Verse is ranked #8, and Wes Anderson's Asteroid City is ranked #6, while his Netflix Roald Dahl short The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar is #35.
Jawan, directed by Atlee and starring Shah Rukh Khan, is ranked #25; it is the highest-grossing Indian release of the year and the second-highest-grossing Hindi film ever.
Anatomy of a Fall, directed by Justine Triet and starring Sandra Hüller, is ranked #20 and described as a Palme d'Or winner; Hüller's performance is called perhaps the year's best by any actor.
Godzilla Minus One, directed by Takashi Yamazaki, is ranked #13 as the first Japanese live-action Godzilla film from Toho since Shin Godzilla.
Shin Kamen Rider, directed by Hideaki Anno, opens the countdown at #50 and is called the best superhero movie of 2023 not made by Marvel or DC.
The honorable mentions, which received votes but missed the top 50, include Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, The Super Mario Bros. Movie, Fast X, The Marvels and Indiana Jones and the Dial of Destiny.
